newsitem.title: CHILE: EU unhappy with Chile whiskey proposals -- Brittan.
newsitem.headline: EU unhappy with Chile whiskey proposals -- Brittan.

text.p: The European Union is not satisfied with proposals by the Chilean government to solve a spat over whiskey taxes and may complain to the World Trade Organization (WTO), said the EU's top trade official Wednesday.
"If the legislation goes ahead in this way, it does not correspond to our complaint and will not resolve the dispute," European Commission vice president Sir Leon Brittan told a news conference.
Brittan was speaking on the third day of an official visit which has included talks with President Eduardo Frei and Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat.
Chile imposed a 70 percent tax on whiskey in 1979 which has been the subject of constant complaints from whiskey producers.
The most vocal supporter of the tax has been the Chilean association of pisco producers. Pisco, a popular local brandy, is taxed at 25 percent.
Although the new law cuts whiskey taxes sharply and raises taxes slightly on most pisco, it does not tax both drinks according to their alcohol strength as required by WTO rules, said Brittan.
If Chile does not present new proposals soon, the EU may file another complaint to the WTO, he said.
"This has been going on too long, we will have to bring the matter to a head," said Brittan.
The EU first filed charges against Chile to the WTO in 1995 charging that the tax on whiskey sales, including the Scotch variety, was a non-tariff trade barrier.
The spat will not affect discussions on extending an existing economic cooperation agreement between Chile and the EU into a full free trade accord, said Brittan.
"It is not an unfriendly act to go to the WTO. It isolates the dispute and stops it spreading to other sectors," he said.
The bloc is one of Chile's largest trading partners, with bilateral trade totalling $7.6 billion in 1995.
Brittan was due to fly to Brazil later this week.
